parallel.requirements: The parallel attempt recognized a clean-room reimplementation task for the Halite-style game engine and investigated CLI behavior, protocol, replay format, dimensions, RNG, terrain, and simulation rules.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent created isolated work directories and delegated five research scopes, while implicitly retaining implementation and final assembly ownership in the main context.
parallel.implementation: Most work remained behavioral probing and spec discovery; late in the run the parent wrote compile.sh and a minimal src/main.cpp that returned immediately rather than a complete engine.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Child work was largely not integrated into a complete implementation; the final archive did include the late skeleton source, compile script, specs, and work artifacts.
parallel.verification: The attempt generated many black-box probes but did not reach an integrated self-test of a full reimplementation before timeout; official evaluation later passed only 32 of 391 cases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The required game engine behavior remained largely absent from the submitted C++ program, and all five child agents were still active near closure.

serial.requirements: The serial attempt recognized the same clean-room reimplementation task and investigated protocol, quiet output, replay structure, map generation, game rules, and timeout behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main actor owned the entire investigation and implementation path, tracked progress with a TodoList, and did not delegate any work.
serial.implementation: The serial trajectory stayed in probing and analysis; it did not create source files or a compile script for the replacement executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The final package contained only the default repository, license, README, and original executable, so there was no original source delivery to integrate or build.
serial.verification: The serial run verified many observed behaviors locally but never ran an integrated replacement because no replacement implementation existed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run ended at timeout with no submitted source or build process, causing official compile_failed and 391 not-run tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the black-box reverse-engineering requirements and split them across CLI, simulation, dimensions, replay, and RNG scopes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same clean-room constraints and broad feature surface but pursued them as one continuous investigation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized the task, but parallel spread requirement discovery across subagents while serial held the requirement model in one trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created five background agents for distinct research topics and kept parent ownership of implementation and final assembly.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegation and used a single TodoList to sequence probing, map-generation work, rules work, implementation, and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel run achieved broader concurrent research but left integration pressure on the parent; serial avoided coordination overhead but never reached implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were scoped by topic, but shared TodoList state leaked across agents and forced actors to distinguish foreign progress state from their own.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial maintained local task state in one actor and updated the same TodoList over time without cross-agent contamination.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an observed tool-state contamination boundary; serial had ordinary single-context progress tracking.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel reached a late C++ build skeleton with compile.sh and src/main.cpp, but the entry point was only a minimal placeholder.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not write source files or a compile script, leaving the packaged artifact without an implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced a buildable but mostly empty replacement; serial produced no replacement implementation at all.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel still had five live subagents late in the parent run, so their full outputs were not joined into a final implementation before cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; its background shell tasks were local probes and the run ended by cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure was complicated by unresolved delegated work; serial closure was a single-agent timeout with no child results to retrieve.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used separate work directories for implementation probes, but TodoList/tool state crossed actor boundaries and polluted progress tracking.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked in one context and its TodoList entries reflected only that actor's own staged work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete shared-state difference is tool-state leakage in parallel, not a filesystem collision; serial lacked that cross-actor state boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran many exploratory probes and later reached official evaluation, but it did not perform a complete integrated replacement verification before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran exploratory probes but had no replacement to compile or evaluate locally; official evaluation failed at compile time.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a compiled partial artifact that could be scored, while serial had only probe evidence and no buildable submission.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel exhausted the agent budget with all five subagents still active, then was cancelled after writing only a minimal skeleton.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but closure came after a single long investigation path and no implementation delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's budget pressure is tied to broad concurrent fan-out; serial's timeout is an ordinary single-threaded research-to-no-delivery failure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is both_fail, not a discordant pass/fail split. Parallel nevertheless delivered a materially different artifact: a package with compile.sh and src/main.cpp that built and reached official scoring, passing 32 of 391. Serial delivered no source or compile script, so the evaluator reported compile_failed and no tests ran.
parallel_contributors: Five-way research fan-out produced broad observations but left final implementation and integration until the end.
The submitted parallel artifact had a build script and source skeleton, allowing partial official evaluation.
serial_contributors: The serial attempt retained all work in one actor and avoided cross-agent coordination errors.
The serial attempt did not transition from probing into source delivery before timeout.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel implemented only a minimal C++ entry point rather than the game engine.
Serial did not implement or package a replacement executable at all.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no official outcome difference; retained labels describe parallel-side adverse process patterns and supported comparative contributors only

candidates.reason: The parent retained implementation ownership and wrote compile.sh plus src/main.cpp; late and incomplete implementation is not ownerless.
The delegated scopes were mostly research probes and did not produce multiple completed components needing an unowned integration step.
The parent wrote the final build script and entry-point source, so assembly was owned even though it was too late and incomplete.
The parent acted as the end-to-end owner across probing, scaffolding, and packaging; the failure was execution capacity, not absent pipeline ownership.
There was no single mandatory serial preflight gate; the parent and children overlapped on multiple investigations and parent-side work.
Parallel investigation did not finish as a complete first phase before implementation; probes, child work, and parent work overlapped until cancellation.
The same allocation chain is more specifically collective fan-out budget exhaustion, not generic starvation of an implementation path.
The parent launched five concurrent research agents, still had all five active late, then wrote only a late build skeleton before cancellation.
candidates.realized_consequence: Broad live research fan-out plus continued parent research consumed the closure budget, leaving only a late build script and stub source instead of an integrated engine.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent continued inspecting and working; the directly evidenced boundary is excessive concurrent breadth rather than passive waiting without inspection.

candidates.reason: No one child was demonstrably overbroad relative to siblings; the budget issue came from the collective breadth of five live research children.
The child briefs were scoped by topic and included environment and acceptance requirements; no already-known omitted requirement made child work unusable.
The children were not assigned separately owned interoperating implementation modules with missing file, API, or data contracts; they mostly produced research probes.
There is no evidence that a known finding was omitted, truncated, or lost in transfer and then caused repeated work by a receiver.
No completed child handoff reached the parent in a too-large or unstructured form that the parent failed to reduce before acting.
No receiver consumed a handoff describing a superseded workspace or decision state and then took an inconsistent action.
No incompatible child reports or contracts reached a parent decision point and remained unadjudicated.
The parent did not make an observable whole-task completion or acceptance decision; evaluator failure alone cannot establish this label.
No replacement or retry actor was launched without inherited findings and then repeated the same work.

candidates.reason: The visible child incompletion is part of the terminal fan-out budget chain; no separate parent decision stopped a specific needed child early.
No complete promotable implementation or mutually compatible component set existed before closure; only partial research and a stub were present.
No child implementation result was merged after integrated verification, and no post-merge verification gap of that form is visible.
No delegated implementation was completed or retrievable and then left unjoined; delegated work was research-heavy and remained active.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; missing aggregate returns are downstream of the fan-out budget episode.
No required child failure, abort, or cancellation produced a separate unfinished scope that the parent visibly refused to resume or reassign.
No completed child result was visible to the parent at a decision point and then ignored while the parent proceeded inconsistently.
The parent checked active task state and continued foreground implementation work; the same closure chain is better captured by fan-out budget exhaustion.
The subagents were directed into isolated work directories and did not produce competing implementation files that claimed overlapping behavior.
There is no evidence that two live agents edited the same source or configuration file and had to reconcile the change.
No actor replaced or deleted non-entry source owned by another actor.
No required executable or entry-point source was overwritten while another actor owned or used that deliverable.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple final-tree outputs and invalidated another actor's work.
Implementation probes used isolated work directories; the retained shared-state event is TodoList/tool-state leakage rather than shared file writes.
Parallel actors consumed shared TodoList/tool state from other concurrent scopes and rewrote or abandoned tracking in response.
candidates.realized_consequence: Foreign TodoList state created coordination noise and repeated progress-tracking rewrites across actors, consuming attention without improving integration.
candidates.near_match_reason: The affected artifact was shared tool state rather than source files, build outputs, or a shared implementation workspace.
